questions.question:
**Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.**

He said to his sister, “Please help me with my homework.”

options.text: His sister told him that he should help her with her homework.
His sister was asked by her brother that she should help him with his homework.
He told his sister that she should help him with his homework.
He requested his sister to help him with his homework.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **He requested his sister to help him with his homework**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
 
 
• The commas, inverted commas are removed.
 
• 'Please' indicates a request and therefore, the **reporting verb** 'requested' should be used in place of 'please' and it **must be** **followed by an object**.
 
• **Requests** are usually **reported using** a **to-infinitive** (here, **to help**).
 
• The **first-person pronoun 'me'** becomes the **third-person pronoun 'him'** and the **first-person pronoun 'my'** becomes the **third-person pronoun 'his'**.

 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य direct speech है।
 
• Direct speech को indirect speech में बदलने के लिए बुनियादी नियम:
 
 
• Commas, inverted commas और exclamation mark हटा दिए जाते हैं।
 
• 'Please' एक अनुरोध को इंगित करता है और इसलिए, 'Please' के स्थान पर रिपोर्टिंग क्रिया 'requested' का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• Requests को आमतौर पर to-infinitive (यहां, to help) का उपयोग करके रिपोर्ट किया जाता है।
 
• First-person pronoun 'me', third-person pronoun 'him' बन जाता है और first-person pronoun 'my', third-person pronoun 'his' बन जाता है।

 
 
 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The patient says, “I am fine.”

options.text: The patient says that he will be fine.
The patient says that he is fine.
The patient says that he would be fine.
The patient says that he was fine.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The patient says that he is fine.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I am fine" becomes "he is fine"**
 
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "he" to reflect the third person in indirect speech.
 
• Verb "am" is changed to "is" to match the subject "he".
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "says"
 
• Remains the same as it is in the present tense.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to a reported clause.
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** The patient says that he is fine.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The patient says that he will be fine. 

 
 
• Changes the meaning to future tense, which is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The patient says that he would be fine. 
 
 
• Uses conditional "would" which changes the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The patient says that he was fine. 
 
 
• Changes the tense to past, which is incorrect.

options.text: The professor said I should learn these words regularly.
The professor said that I had to learn those words regularly.
The professor said that I must learn these words regularly.
The professor said that you had to learn these words regularly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To **convert it into indirect speech**, we need to make the necessary changes:
 
• **Change the pronoun** "you" to the appropriate pronoun based on the context.
 
• Since the professor said the statement, we** can assume** that the person being addressed is the person reporting the statement.
 
• Therefore, **"you" **changes to **"I" **in the indirect form.
 
• Change the verb form from** "must"** to a verb form that reflects indirect speech. In this case, **"must"** changes to **"had to"** in the indirect form.
 
• Add the conjunction **"that"** to introduce the reported statement.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* The professor said that I had to learn those words regularly.*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, “I will go to Indonesia tomorrow”.

options.text: He said that he would go to Indonesia tomorrow.
He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day.
He said that he would be going to Indonesia the next day.
He said he would go to Indonesia by tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **When converting** direct speech into indirect or reported speech, certain rules need to be followed.
 
• For instance, **verb tenses** usually **shift back** in reported speech.
 
• The present tense** becomes **the past tense, future tense **changes** to conditional tense.
 
• **He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day: **This option** correctly converts **"will go" to "would go" and "tomorrow" to "the next day". 
 
• It is a **correct transformation **of the direct speech into indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Given this, let's analyze the options:
 
 
• **He said that he would go to Indonesia tomorrow: **This option **incorrectly** retains "tomorrow". In **reported speech,** "tomorrow" should become** "the next day".**
 
• **He said that he would be going to Indonesia the next day:** While this sentence is grammatically correct, it is a slightly more elaborate way of expressing the future in the past. The simpler form ("would go") is usually preferred.
 
• **He said he would go to Indonesia by tomorrow:** This option changes the meaning of the original sentence. "By tomorrow" implies he will go sometime before or at the designated time (tomorrow), which is not what the original sentence says.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

She said to her maid, "Clean the utensils properly."

options.text: She ordered her maid to clean the utensils properly.
She commanded her maid that kindly clean the utensils properly.
She orders her maid to clean the utensils properly.
She commands her maid that clean the utensils properly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'She ordered her maid to clean the utensils properly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct indirect form** of the sentence* "She said to her maid, 'Clean the utensils properly.'*" is *"She ordered her maid to clean the utensils properly."*
 
• In the **direct sentence,** the speaker is giving an order or command.
 
• Therefore, in the indirect form, we use the verb** "ordered"** to reflect this.
 
• **We also change the sentence structure** to follow the pattern: *"She + ordered + her maid + to-infinitive (to clean)".*
 
• The words inside the quotes are changed from direct speech to indirect speech without the quotes.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is: *"She ordered her maid to clean the utensils properly."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's look at the incorrect options:
 
 
• *Option 2 "She commanded her maid that kindly clean the utensils properly."* - this sentence is grammatically incorrect as it does not correctly follow the pattern for reported commands. We wouldn't use "that" after "commanded" in this context.
 
• *Option 3 "She orders her maid to clean the utensils properly."* - This sentence changes the tense from past (said) to present (orders), which is not accurate for reported speech.
 
• *Option 4 "She commands her maid that clean the utensils properly." -* This is incorrect for the same reason as option 2: it incorrectly uses "that" after "commands".

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“I have heard the podcast before,” Nita says.

options.text: Nita says that she is hearing the podcast before.
Nita says that she had heard the podcast before.
Nita says that she has heard the podcast before.
Nita says that she had heard the podcast ago.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, Nita's **experience of having heard** the podcast before is still a relevant fact when she is reporting it, so the **present perfect tense** ("has heard") will be retained in the reported speech.
 
• When the Direct Speech is in **Present Tense** (in this case, 'says') or **Future Tense,** there is** no change** in the Indirect Speech.
 
• **'Has'** will be used instead of **'Have'** as we use '**Has'** with singular noun or singular pronoun.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Nita says that she has heard the podcast before.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Nita says that she is hearing the podcast before."** : This is incorrect because "is hearing" is present continuous tense, which doesn't fit the meaning of the sentence, and "before" can't be used with this tense in this context.
 
• **"Nita says that she had heard the podcast before."** : This is not incorrect, but it's more common to use "has heard" in this context for the reasons explained above.
 
• **"Nita says that she had heard the podcast ago."** : This is incorrect because "ago" is not used with the past perfect tense. It's used with the past simple tense to indicate how much time has passed since an event. Also, the word "before" is missing from the sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of given sentence.**

The foreigner said to the farmer, “Can you tell me the way to the nearest hotel?”

options.text: The foreigner exclaimed with the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner suggested the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner told the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While changing the narration of an **interrogative sentence**, we need to follow the given steps-

 
 
• The conjunction **‘if’ **should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”).
 
• **'Question mark (?)'** is changed to full stop **(.).**
 
• **‘Said to’ **will be changed into **‘asked’**.
 
• **'Can' **is changed to **'could'.**
 
• **2nd person **(you) is changed into **he** and **1st person **(me) is changed into **him** i.e.according to the **object** (farmer) and the **subject** (foreigner) of the **reporting verb** respectively.

 
 
 

**The final sentence-** *The foreigner asked the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.*

• When converting direct speech into indirect speech, the tense of the verbs usually shifts back (this is known as "backshifting").
 
• In this case, the** past simple tense** "was" **changes to **the past perfect tense "had been."
 
• This shift accurately conveys the timing of the events in the indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *'Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day.'*

• **"Miranda told her teacher that she is sick for a day."** - This is incorrect because the present tense "is" doesn't accurately represent the past events conveyed in the original direct speech.
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she was sick for a day." **- Although it might seem correct in some contexts, in proper English grammar, while changing from direct to indirect speech, the tense usually shifts back. Therefore, "was" should become "had been."
